questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code caches and evaluates feature flags when the flag service is slow or unavailable? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The flag service starts failing 2 minutes after a successful load. A request arrives at that moment, finding the cache expired. Which description of what happens is correct?
choices: The request raises FlagsUnavailable because the TTL has passed
Every concurrent request makes its own fetch call and each waits for its own timeout
The request returns each flag's DEFAULTS value immediately
The request waits up to the fetch timeout, then uses the flags from 2 minutes ago, and calls in the next 5 seconds skip the fetch

questions.prompt: The flag service stays down for 10 minutes. What does is_enabled("block-new-card-bins", ...) return?
choices: False, because failures fail closed to disabled
True, from the hardcoded default, once the snapshot is more than 300s old
The last known value forever, because the snapshot is never discarded

questions.prompt: Compared with refreshing the cache outside the lock, what is the main tradeoff of this design when the cache expires under heavy traffic?
choices: Many threads can refresh at once, multiplying load on the flag service
Stale values can be served indefinitely
Callers can be delayed for up to the fetch timeout, but only one fetch call is in flight
Flag values can differ between threads in the same instant
